armoury_crate._comment: Writes sent by Armoury Crate on Windows 11, captured with USBPcap 2026-11-12 (ROG Omni receiver, endpoint 0x03 OUT / 0x83 IN = interface 2, report ID 03). Each OUT packet was echoed unchanged on 0x83. Armoury Crate sent no reads in the capture: it writes from its own cached state. Not used by Squire yet; documentation for the next writes (not approved, see CLAUDE.md Rules).

captures.name: DPI stage 3: 650 -> 700, Apply
captures.notes: One Apply rewrites the whole sensor block, then saves. 51 31 0b = angle tuning 0 and 51 31 06 = angle snapping off (same bytes as G-Helper); 51 31 04 00 03 = polling index 3 = 1000 Hz (reads back as 0x63: the high nibble is not part of the write); 51 31 0a 00 04 = 4 stages on the DPI button; 51 31 09 00 03 = active stage, same value as 12 00 [11] (1-based: stage 3 is active afterwards, it was 4); 51 31 <stage 0-based> 00 <lo> <hi> <r g b> = DPI (v*50+50, sets X and Y alike, 12 04 02 reads 0d 00 0d 00) plus the stage colour (12 04 03). No debounce (51 31 05) and no lift-off write. Active stage 4 -> 3: the owner had to select stage 3 in Armoury Crate to edit it. Side effects the owner did not choose: angle snapping on -> off and the colour of stage 3 #000000 -> #003dff, both from Armoury Crate's own state (it overwrites values changed by other tools without reading them first). Mouse firmware 01.00.10 and receiver 07.00.08 at the time (the owner updated both in Armoury Crate the same day, from 01.00.09 / 07.00.02); all reads parse the same with the new firmware.

captures.name: lift-off low -> high (surface ROG Sheath)
captures.notes: Owner had selected the surface ROG Sheath in Armoury Crate before (not captured), then switched lift-off to high. Write (relative to 51): [2..3] 00 00, [4] surface id 01 = ROG Sheath, [5] lift-off 01 = high, [6] 00 (the echo returns 01 here: ack?), [7..9] surface parameters 1c 34 16 (from Armoury Crate's surface list, no calibration was run). Read 12 06 (relative to 12): [4] 01, [5] 00, [6] surface id, [7] lift-off, [8..10] the same parameters. On 2026-11-10 (no surface selected) 12 06 read [4] 00, [5..6] ff ff, [7] 00, [8..10] 00: surface ff = none. G-Helper writes 51 35 ff 00 ff <lift-off>, i.e. surface ff without parameters: that is why it 'resets the calibration'. A safe lift-off write keeps [6] and [8..10] from a 12 06 read.

captures.name: surface ROG Sheath -> Balteus Qi
captures.notes: Owner selected the surface Balteus Qi only: surface id 0b, parameters 1a 32 20. Armoury Crate also set lift-off back to low (00) without being asked; its UI shows low too. So a surface change in Armoury Crate resets lift-off.

capture_4._comment: Fourth Armoury Crate capture session, Windows, USBPcap via the Omni, 2026-11-22: one change at a time, in the order the owner reported. Each write was echoed and followed by 50 55 (also echoed). Facts only; vendor endpoints (OUT 03 / IN 83) only, the .pcapng stays out of the repo. Before: profile 4, reactive, sleep 3 min, warning 20 %.

warning_levels._comment: Block 1: AC offers exactly 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 % and 'never' for the keyboard's low-battery warning. 'Never' is 00. On opening the page AC read 02 12 03 00, 02 12 01 and the mouse (03 12 00 02, 03 12 07). The 30 % write was answered by one ff aa first, then the echo.

writes.name: warning never
writes.notes: 'Never' = 00 (not ff like the sleep timeout).

effect_options._comment: Block 2 (owner picked green as the background). Layout of the single-colour effects with options (indices from 51): [6] colour mode: 00 single, 10 double, 01 random; [7..8] ff ff; [9..11] colour 1; [12..14] colour 2 (00 00 00 in single mode; switching to double, AC sent colour 1 ff 00 00 and colour 2 ff 00 ff); [15..17] background colour (00 00 00 in AC's default = background off; turning it on sent ff ff ff, then the picked green). Random keeps both colours in the packet. Same layout for starry night (06), current (08) and raindrop (09). Starry night already had double + a blue background in AC when its first write went out. Turning the background off again was not captured: assumed 00 00 00 like the default.

speeds._comment: Block 3: background off (raindrop, random mode: [15..17] 00 00 00, confirms block 2), then fast / normal / slow per effect, in that order (owner). Selecting an effect first sent AC's cached speed, which was 'normal' every time. Speed byte [4] (from 51) per effect, fast / normal / slow: reactive 08 / 0f / 16; starry night 0a / 0f / 19; current 07 / 0a / 0c; colour cycle 12 / 1f / 3e; rainbow 23 / 3e / 55; ripple 50 / 64 / 78; quicksand 0c / 0f / 14 (earlier: breathing 0f / 1e / 2a, raindrop 0e / 14 / 1b). Larger = slower for every effect; no common scale. Gradient effects resend all chunks with only the speed changed. Rainbow's direction byte [7] was 08 here (AC's cached direction; 00 and 04 known from capture_2). Only the first chunk of each gradient / quicksand write is listed; the other chunks were unchanged (see capture_3).

rainbow._comment: Block 4, rainbow (04). Gradient layout confirmed (indices from 51): chunk 02: [4] speed, [5] brightness %, [6] 00, [7] direction, [8] 02 (unknown, maybe AC's 'thickness'), [9] stop count, then stops of 4 bytes <position %> <r g b>: 2 stops in chunk 02 ([10..17]), up to 4 in chunk 01 ([4..19]), the rest in chunk 00 ([4..]). Unused chunks are sent as zeros. AC's gradient presets have no names (owner; screenshot: 7 presets, a separator, then the custom gradient). Presets in AC's order: 1 red (2 stops), 2 blue -> red (2), 3 orange / pink / red (3, the one in capture_2), 4 lime / cyan / cyan / lime (4), 5 yellow / magenta alternating (5), 6 pink / purple (6), 7 spectrum = AC default (7). The first stop is at 14 % (0e) in every preset, the last at 100 % (64). Direction [7]: AC shows 9 buttons (up, down, left, right, four diagonals, and 'from the centre outwards, left/right', the one selected at the start = 08). The owner clicked them in display order; packets: 06, 02, 04, 00, 05, 07, 03, 01, 08. So 00 right (= left -> right, known), 02 down, 04 left (= right -> left, known), 06 up; odd values are diagonals (assumed 01 down-right, 03 down-left, 05 up-left, 07 up-right, i.e. 45 degree steps clockwise from 'right'); 08 centre outwards. Custom gradient: the owner changed stop colours (stop 1 -> 65 00 ff, stop 4 -> eb f5 eb, stop 6 -> 3d ff 00); positions and stop count stayed (7 stops).

writes.name: custom: stop 4 colour eb f5 eb (chunk 01)
custom: stop 6 colour 3d ff 00 (chunk 01; chunk 00 unchanged)

thickness_ripple_quicksand._comment: Block 5. Thickness (AC setting for rainbow and ripple) = byte [8] of chunk 02 (from 51), 3 steps 00 / 01 / 02 in AC's order (02 = AC default, the '02' seen in every earlier gradient capture). Removing a stop: stop count [9] 07 -> 06, the remaining stops are packed again (the 100 % stop moved from chunk 00 into chunk 01, chunk 00 sent as zeros). Dragging a stop changes only its position byte (48 -> 53, 72 % -> 83 %). Ripple: same gradient layout and presets, [7] = ff (no direction), thickness [8] 00 / 01 / 02 like rainbow. Quicksand (two chunks, from 51): [6] 00 colour scale / 01 random (the 6 colours are still sent), [7] direction 02 down (AC default) / 06 up: the same compass coding as rainbow's direction (02 down, 06 up). Speed 14 (slow) was left from block 3.

writes.name: rainbow: stop 5 dragged 72 % -> 83 % (chunk 01; chunk 02 as above, chunk 00 zero)

brightness_off._comment: Block 6, brightness and lighting off (owner). AC's brightness is a slider 0..100 % in steps of 5; it is byte [5] of 51 2c in percent (static green 00 ff 00 seen at 100, 85, 65, 10, 0, 65; 0 was answered by one ff aa first, then echoed). AC has no per-key or per-zone mode for the Falchion (G-Helper has one, owner). AC's 'lighting off' switch for the keyboard sent, in this order: 03 51 36 00 00 01 to the MOUSE (report ID 03; unknown command, not in G-Helper's Keris code as far as known; the mouse LEDs were unchanged afterwards, Squire read: breathing on all three zones), then 02 51 2c 00 00 ff 04 00 ff ff 00 00 00 = static, brightness 4 %, colour black. So AC turns the keyboard lighting 'off' with a black static effect, not with an own effect id; 12 00 [9] then reads 00 static. Thickness names in AC (block 5): 00 Low / Gering, 01 Normal, 02 Strong / Stark.

writes.name: lighting off, part 1 (to the mouse, unknown)

restore._comment: Block 7, lighting on again and restore (owner). Turning AC's lighting switch on sent only 02 51 2c with AC's last cached effect (static green 65 %), nothing to the mouse (no 51 36 counterpart). Then reactive (AC's cached colour 00 02 ff, slow 16) at 100 % and 75 %, normal speed 0f, and the warning back to 20 %. Squire read afterwards: reactive, sleep 3 min, warning 20 %. Note: the owner's earlier colour #f6f5f4 was set by Squire on Linux; AC did not know it and sent its own cached blue.

writes.name: lighting on: AC's cached static green 65 %
